subject: general
question: Select the correct example for mechanical barrier method of contraception from the options given below.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Condom use**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Condoms** are a mechanical barrier method of contraception.
 
• They are designed to prevent sperm from entering the uterus and thus prevent fertilization.
 
• Condoms are available for both males and females, though male condoms are more commonly used.
 
• This method is not only effective in preventing pregnancy but also in protecting against sexually transmitted infections (STIs).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Male Sterilization**

 
 
• Also known as a vasectomy, it is a permanent method of contraception for men.
 
• It involves cutting or sealing the vas deferens, which are the tubes that carry sperm from the testicles to the urethra.
 
• While effective, it is not considered a mechanical barrier method.
 
 
 
• **Use of Copper-T**
 
 
• It is an intrauterine device (IUD) that is inserted into the uterus to prevent pregnancy.
 
• The copper ions released by the device are toxic to sperm and egg, preventing fertilization.
 
• This method is a form of long-term contraception but not a mechanical barrier method.
 
 
 
• **Use of Birth Control Pills**
 
 
• These are hormonal contraceptives taken orally by women.
 
• They work by preventing ovulation, thickening cervical mucus, and thinning the uterine lining.
 
• While effective, they are not considered a mechanical barrier method.
